titre: Enrolling my child in the school canteen and after-school care
resume: Who runs the canteen in primary school, middle school and high school, the documents to prepare to get the right rate, and where to ask for help if the cost is a problem.
aQuoiCaSert: The canteen and périscolaire (before- and after-school care, supervised homework, activities) mean your child is looked after around school hours. In nursery and primary school, the town (commune) runs them and sets the prices, often based on your family quotient (quotient familial, a family income index calculated by the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office)): without a quotient certificate, you may pay the highest rate. In middle and high school (collège and lycée), you enroll for school lunches (demi-pension) with the school itself.
quiEstConcerne: Parents of children in nursery or primary school.
Parents of middle and high school students, for school lunches (demi-pension).
Parents of a child with an allergy or on a special diet for health reasons.
aSavoir: The canteen is not compulsory, in primary or secondary school. But where one exists, every child in school has the right to be enrolled: the parents' social situation cannot prevent it, and restricting access to children whose parents work is illegal.

Prices are set by the town for primary schools, by the conseil départemental (département council) for middle schools and by the region for high schools. Each can apply a family quotient to adapt the price to your income.
Some towns, départements or regions also grant canteen support. In some départements, support also exists for a child whose primary school is far from home and who must have lunch there.
In middle and high school, the canteen social fund (fonds social pour les cantines) can help families. It is granted by the head of the school, who sets out the conditions at the start of the year.

Allergy or diet for health reasons: an individualized care plan (projet d'accueil individualisé, PAI) can be set up with the doctor. You can also provide a packed lunch, for which you are then responsible (meal, packaging, transport).

Separated parents: enrolling in the canteen is part of the child's everyday life. If you have shared residence, ask the town hall (mairie) whether each parent can be billed for their own weeks, and with which family quotient.

documents.detail: Free download from your Caf account (Mon compte, Attestations). Without it, the maximum rate may apply.
Copy. Often requested if you do not receive Caf benefits. Downloadable on impots.gouv.fr.
Copy. Bill or rent receipt in your name.

documents.libelle: ID of the parent enrolling the child
documents.detail: Original or copy, depending on the town hall.

documents.libelle: Family record book (livret de famille) or the child's birth certificate
documents.detail: Copy. Birth certificate free online on service-public.gouv.fr.
Often required for the canteen and after-school care. Ask your home or school insurer.

documents.libelle: Vaccination pages of the health record book
documents.detail: Copy, often requested for after-school care.

documents.libelle: Individual care plan (PAI) and medical certificate, if needed
documents.detail: To prepare with your doctor and the school management before the first meal.

documents.libelle: Judgment or residence agreement, if you are separated
documents.detail: Copy. Useful for billing under shared residence and for the list of people allowed to pick up the child.
If you choose automatic direct debit.

etapes.detail: In primary school, ask the town hall's school or after-school service. In middle and high school, ask the school office or the bursar's office (intendance). Ask for the enrollment dates, the list of documents and the price list.
Family quotient certificate on caf.fr, tax notice on impots.gouv.fr, insurance certificate from your insurer.

Family quotient certificate, proof of address, ID, family record book, insurance certificate, vaccination pages, PAI if needed, judgment if separated, RIB for direct debit. Note which days your child will attend.
At the counter or on the town's family portal (portail famille) if there is one. Specify the canteen and after-school care days.

In primary school, ask at the town hall or the school social worker. In middle and high school, ask the social worker or the school office about the canteen social fund, and check your département's or region's website.
Log each payment in your Journal to keep a history of your child's expenses and make sharing costs with the other parent easier.

aConfirmer: To be confirmed locally: prices, required documents, family portal and how after-school care is organized, specific to each town.
To be confirmed at the town hall: some towns apply a social canteen rate (meals at €1 or less for low-income families) with State support; this is not the case everywhere.
To be confirmed locally: school lunch (demi-pension) prices, support from the département or region, and the social fund calendar, to ask the school about.
To be confirmed locally: billing under shared residence (one bill per parent or not), depending on the town.
